newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain spread over Bunds seen staying below 135 bps.
newsitem.headline: Spain spread over Bunds seen staying below 135 bps.

text.p: The sharp sell-off in peripheral European bond markets in recent days should be bottoming out, analysts said on Wednesday.
They expected Spain's 10-year bond spread over Bunds to trade under 135 basis points for the next two weeks, with a widening to 150 basis points in the worst case scenario.

"With the new 7.35-percent (bono) benchmark, the spread might find an upward limit of 135 basis points, while the old one (with the 8.80 percent 10-year bond) has a maximum of ten points lower," said an analyst who declined to be named. Remarks over a possible Italy and Spain's possible delay into European economic and monetary union (EMU) caused the spread to widen in the past month.
It hit a record low of about 85 basis points (bps) on January 22. By Tuesday, it had widened to 130 bps, although around 10 basis points was attributed to changes in benchmarks.
"The worsening of the spread has to do with the market starting to consider the possibility of a delay in EMU," said Carmen Hernansanz, economist at Merrill Lynch.
The market's focus has shifted from how and whether peripherals are meeting Maastricht criteria to how Germany is doing, given its high jobless rate, she said.

German unemployment surged in January to 4.66 million people, the highest level since 1933. For Spain, prospects for the whole EMU project being delayed would be worse than if its individual entry suffered a setback.

"At this point, the fact that Spain will meet the criteria is almost known...Spain could be among the most penalised if the project were delayed," said Luca Jellinek, analyst at Paribas Capital Markets in London.
Jellinek said it is difficult to predict where the 10-year spread might go because "often the market overdoes it, and it could reach 150 basis points."
But other economists saw the current correction ending soon.
"We've seen unwinding of long positions out of peripherals and toward dollar assets, but this movement is likely to end soon" said Jose Luis Alzola at Salomon Brother in London.
The peseta was likely to remain below the key level of 85.00 per mark, while the 10-year spread should remain where its is trading now, he added.
At around 1440 GMT, the 10-year spread over Bunds was trading at 125 basis points.
